## K7 · k7-f1-pid-double-count — K7 F1: a created process counts twice against PID limits

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 4

Decision references: docs/kernel/processes.md, docs/kernel/budgets.md#r6-charging

Evidence: Architect decided: single count per held PID (creator's limit for created processes, running budget for loader-started ones); written on docs/kernel/processes.md, docs/kernel/budgets.md R6 and docs/todo/pid-pool-pinning.md, committed 068a3e6ff; K7 builds it in G2.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `5fd0759395f9aaa356b827e48aed11d1` · 2026-09-28T02:31:51Z

> K7 F1, K7-plan.md 'F1 (pid-pool)' on docs/todo/pid-pool-pinning.md: the page's rule counts a created process twice, once in the budget it runs in while it lives and once as an object in its creator's budget until freed. With root's 62 PIDs the machine then holds only about 31 created processes. The implementer says every alternative it checked leaks PIDs, and will follow the page. M1 needs ~10 servers plus sessions, beamlet VMs and an agent, so halving capacity matters. Is the double count the intended rule, or should the object count replace the running count (or the running count be bounded some other way)? Decide, write it on docs/kernel/processes.md / budgets.md R6 as needed, and answer on the thread.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `6bfb2255e434c9d483aedefdfca9ddc5` · 2026-09-28T02:36:44Z

> Decided: the double count was not intended. The object count replaces the running count. Not an owner choice: no wall moves, and budgets.md Why already says processes are counted apart "only because PIDs are … scarce".
> 
> Rule: a process limit counts PIDs, and every held PID counts once.
> - A created process counts against its creator's process limit from process_create until its object is freed, which is exactly its PID's lifetime. It does not count again in the budget it runs in; that budget's pages already bound what runs there.
> - A program the loader started has no object, so it counts in the budget it runs in while it lives, and its PID goes when it ends.
> - All limits are carved from root's 63 (every PID but the kernel's), so a caller under its own limit always finds a free PID, and no budget can take another's. Capacity is back to about 62; nothing leaks, since destroying the creator frees the objects (R10).
> 
> Written (main checkout, unstaged):
> - docs/kernel/processes.md: the Creating and starting counting paragraph states the rule and its reason; process_create's refusal names the caller's limit; teardown drops "stops counting at once". The departure sentence stays, since the kernel is unchanged.
> - docs/kernel/budgets.md: the `processes` field row, the R6 process-object bullet and the Failure-and-restart bullet state the rule (with the departure). Why: "the count follows the PID, once per PID held".
> - docs/todo/pid-pool-pinning.md: What quotes the new rule and says why not both. Done when adds single counting, the limit check before the PID draw, and the ABI row, error table and model-disagreement residual updated with the code.
> I left docs/kernel/abi.md alone: it records the kernel's order ("the table above is the kernel's"), so K7 changes it with the code.
> 
> Checks: mdbook build docs exit 0; cargo run -q -p redoubt-doccheck exit 0.
> 
> For K7: moving the PID draw after the limit check also ends abi.md's process_create kernel/model disagreement.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `51a664650ea82ea68405bc48d66900b1` · 2026-09-28T02:36:52Z

> F1 decided: no double count. A process limit counts PIDs, once per held PID: a created process counts against its creator's limit from process_create until its object is freed, and NOT again in the budget it runs in; a loader-started program (no object) counts where it runs while it lives. Capacity stays ~62. Written on docs/kernel/processes.md, docs/kernel/budgets.md (R6) and docs/todo/pid-pool-pinning.md (Done when adds: single counting, the limit check before the PID draw, and abi.md's process_create row, error table and model-disagreement residual updated with the code; abi.md is yours to change with the code). Committed on redoubt; rebase between groups. Do it in G2.
